hero.subtitle: Whether it happened on Ygnacio Valley Road, I-680, or a side street near downtown, a Walnut Creek car accident leaves you with questions before the tow truck has even left. We handle these claims and can help you understand what comes next.

about.title: Walnut Creek Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Walnut Creek is a pass-through point for much of Contra Costa County, and I-680 carries a steady stream of commuters straight through the middle of town. Public records for 2025 list 310 injury collisions inside city limits, with 413 people hurt and 5 lives lost. Ygnacio Valley Road, I-680, N Main Street, and Treat Boulevard account for the largest share of those reports, and Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. show the week's highest counts. Behind each number is a person sorting out what comes next: medical bills, a car in the shop, missed shifts, and calls from an adjuster who works for the other driver. Our team handles car accident claims in Contra Costa County. You tell us what happened; we review your situation and guide you through the process. We work on contingency, meaning no fee unless your claim recovers money. Reaching out costs nothing and commits you to nothing.

whyChoose.title: What We Bring to a Walnut Creek Car Accident Claim

items.title: Deadlines that arrive sooner than people expect
items.desc: California generally gives you two years to file a car accident lawsuit, but if a city, county, or state agency is involved, a claim may need to be filed in as little as six months. We sort out which clock applies to your situation early, before options quietly close.

items.title: Being partly at fault does not end your claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so you can still recover even if you share some blame, with your recovery reduced by your percentage of fault. There is also no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost quality of life in an ordinary car accident case, which is exactly why insurers push hard on the fault question.

items.title: Protecting evidence and handling the insurer for you
items.desc: Photos, dashcam footage, witness contacts, and repair records fade fast, and the other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement designed to shrink your claim. Our team preserves what matters and speaks to the adjuster so you do not have to, with no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I was rear-ended on I-680 near the Ygnacio Valley Road exit. Does it matter that it was a freeway?
items.answer: It can. Freeway crashes often involve multiple vehicles, CHP reports rather than Walnut Creek police reports, and sometimes questions about road conditions or signage that point toward a public agency. If a government entity might share responsibility, a claim may need to be filed within six months rather than the usual two years. We can look at where the crash happened and who was involved to figure out which rules and deadlines apply.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and most attorneys advise against it. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that make an injury sound minor or shift fault onto you, and anything you say can be used to lower what they offer. It is generally wiser to let us handle those conversations on your behalf.

items.question: The police report says I was partly to blame. Can I still bring a claim?
items.answer: Yes. California uses pure comparative fault, which means a shared-blame finding reduces your recovery by your percentage of fault but does not erase it. A police report is also one piece of evidence, not the final word, and we often challenge fault assessments using photos, witness accounts, and vehicle damage. Contacting us costs nothing, so it is worth finding out where you actually stand.
